German Modal Verbs: A1 Present-Tense Practice

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

A1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

A modal verb agrees with the subject and normally occupies the finite-verb position. The main action stays in the infinitive at the end: Lara kann gut tanzen. The ich and er/sie/es forms have no usual -e or -t ending: ich kann, er kann.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not conjugate both verbs: Lara kann tanzen, not Lara kann tanzt. Müssen means necessity; dürfen expresses permission.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Lara kann sehr gut tanzen.Lara can dance very well.
Worked example 2Wir müssen die Küche aufräumen.We have to tidy the kitchen.
Worked example 3Mein Onkel will ein Boot kaufen.My uncle wants to buy a boat.
Worked example 4Ihr dürft hier fotografieren.You all are allowed to take photos here.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Conjugate the modal verb in brackets in the present tense. Leave the final infinitive unchanged. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Du ___ heute länger schlafen. (dürfen)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: darfst

Dürfen changes to darf- in the singular; du takes darfst.

Question 2. Ich ___ einen Kuchen backen. (wollen)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: will

The ich form of wollen is will, with no -e ending.

Question 3. Die Gäste ___ draußen warten. (müssen)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: müssen

A plural subject takes müssen; warten stays in the infinitive.

Question 4. Mina ___ drei Sprachen sprechen. (können)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: kann

Third-person singular können becomes kann.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
